name: Social Studies: All Together (Grade 1, Scott Foresman / Pearson Education pupil edition, copyright 2003)

layer1_philosophy.methodology: A published, reading-skill-integrated elementary social studies textbook. Each of its 6 units opens with a 'Vocabulary Preview' (one large illustrated scene labeled with the unit's key terms) and names one 'Reading Social Studies' target comprehension skill for the whole unit (Use Picture Clues, Alike and Different, Put Things in Order, Find the Main Idea, Recall and Retell, Predict). Every lesson is short (1-2 pages, a few short declarative sentences, 1-2 bolded vocabulary words) and closes with a fixed 'What Did You Learn?' box: two literal recall questions plus a third open 'Think and Share' or 'Write and Share' question that is usually the actual practice of that unit's named reading skill. Unlike the sibling Harcourt Science volume in this drop wave, there is no hands-on 'Investigate' step anywhere and no fixed process-skills vocabulary; the organizing thread is a reading-comprehension skill applied to social studies content, not a science process skill applied through experimentation.
principles: 6 units, each opening with a 'Begin with a Song' (lyrics set to a familiar tune, for example 'We Go to School' sung to 'The Farmer in the Dell'), then a Vocabulary Preview scene, then a named 'Reading Social Studies' target skill taught in a short worked example before the unit's lessons begin: Unit 1 Time for School (Use Picture Clues), Unit 2 In My Community (Alike and Different), Unit 3 Work! Work! Work! (Put Things in Order), Unit 4 Our Earth, Our Resources (Find the Main Idea), Unit 5 This Is Our Country (Recall and Retell), Unit 6 Our Country, Our World (Predict)

Every lesson (28 across the book) is 1-2 pages of plain declarative text with 1-2 bolded vocabulary words defined in-line (for example 'A community is a group of people and the place where they live'), almost always paired with photographs of real children and real places rather than illustration, and closes with a fixed 'What Did You Learn?' box: 2 literal recall questions, then a 3rd 'Think and Share' or 'Write and Share' open question that practices that unit's named reading skill

A dense rotation of named recurring feature boxes interleaves with the plain lesson content, each with its own distinct job: 'Citizen Heroes' and 'Meet [Person]' Read-Together Biography spreads pair a short real person's story (Ruby Bridges Hall, Mary McLeod Bethune, Jane Addams, Clara Barton, George Washington Carver, Benjamin Franklin, Abraham Lincoln, Eleanor Roosevelt, Mae Jemison, and others) with one named citizenship trait (caring, respect, responsibility, fairness, honesty, courage) and a reflection question; 'Then and Now' compares something across time (a community, toys, a country's flag) in two small panels; 'Map and Globe Skills' and 'Chart and Graph Skills' teach one concrete skill in a small callout separate from the lesson (use a map key, use four directions, follow a route, locate land and water, use a history map, read a calendar, read a time line, read a bar graph, read a diagram); 'Here and There' makes one specific comparison to another place in the world (money around the world, endangered animals, when it is time to leave for school); DK (Dorling Kindersley) inserts are a real-world photo-essay page on one topic (Chinese New Year, telephones, big wheeled vehicles)

A dedicated front-matter 'Social Studies Handbook' (H2-H14, unpaginated with the main book) teaches citizenship vocabulary (respect, caring, responsibility, fairness, honesty, courage, each with a one-line kid-facing definition and photo), a 6-step problem-solving process and a 5-step decision-making process under 'Citizenship in Action', the Five Themes of Geography (Location, Place, Movement, Region, Human-Environment Interaction, called 'Places and People Change Each Other' here) illustrated with one shared example (a school), and a Map and Globe Skills Review page, all taught once before Unit 1 begins the same way the sibling Harcourt Science volume front-loads its process-skills vocabulary

Each unit closes with an 'End with a Poem' (or Song, Legend, or Folktale) tied to the unit's theme, then a Unit Review, then a 'Discovery Channel School' page (a television-themed spread naming a companion video segment, for example 'Jobs in Your Community' or 'Weather Report'; not itself a printable activity)

A combined back-matter 'Reference Guide' (R2-R28) functions as an ongoing whole-year reference the same way the sibling Harcourt Science volume's References section does: an Atlas (satellite photo of Earth, world map, United States map, all-50-states map), a short Geography Terms glossary, a Picture Glossary (roughly 90 terms A-Z, each with one photo example and a page cross-reference back into the lesson content, for example 'community: A group of people and the place where they live. My community is the United States of America. (page 16)'), and an Index
layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: reading-comprehension-skill-integrated, explain-then-practice (the lesson states the concept directly in a few plain sentences, then the child immediately practices a named comprehension skill, predict, sequence, compare, find the main idea, recall and retell, on that same content in the closing 'What Did You Learn?' box), distinct from the sibling Harcourt Science volume's hands-on-first investigate-then-explain sequence: there is no materials-list activity step anywhere in this book
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: lesson-ending-comprehension-check ('What Did You Learn?': 2 recall questions plus 1 open Think-and-Share or Write-and-Share reading-skill question) plus a Unit Review at the close of each of the 6 units; no separate tests, quizzes, or scores observed in any sampled page. The Reference Guide (Atlas, Geography Terms, Picture Glossary, Index) functions as an ongoing reference the child returns to, not a graded checkpoint, the same pattern as the sibling Harcourt Science volume
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: facilitator-and-co-reader (reads or shares the short lesson text, asks the closing What Did You Learn? questions aloud, and helps the child connect Citizen Heroes and Here and There features to their own community)

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Reading-Skill-Integrated Elementary Social Studies (Published Textbook Comprehension Method)
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A published-textbook approach to elementary social studies where each unit teaches one named reading-comprehension skill (predict, alike and different, put things in order, find the main idea, recall and retell, use picture clues) through a Vocabulary Preview scene, then applies that same skill in every lesson's closing 'What Did You Learn?' box (2 recall questions plus 1 open reading-skill question). There is no hands-on investigation step anywhere. Distinct recurring feature boxes each carry one job: Citizen Heroes and Meet-the-Person biographies pair a real person's story with a named citizenship trait; Then and Now compares something across time; Map and Globe Skills and Chart and Graph Skills teach one concrete skill each in a small callout; Here and There makes a single world comparison. This is a distinct methodology from Direct Instruction (no script, no choral response), from the sibling Investigate-Then-Explain science pattern (no hands-on materials-list step; the organizing thread is a reading skill, not a process skill), and from Charlotte Mason (feature boxes and a fixed comprehension-check structure carry the content, not living books and free narration), even though a family may use any of these for different subjects in the same week.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Social Studies: All Together Grade 1 Pupil Edition Format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A Grade 1 elementary social studies pupil edition (Scott Foresman, an imprint of Pearson Education, copyright 2003, ISBN 0-328-01759-0) organized into 6 units (Time for School; In My Community; Work! Work! Work!; Our Earth, Our Resources; This Is Our Country; Our Country, Our World), each with 4-6 lessons plus recurring feature boxes (Citizen Heroes, Then and Now, Map and Globe Skills, Chart and Graph Skills, Here and There, DK inserts). A front-matter Social Studies Handbook (H2-H14) teaches citizenship vocabulary, problem-solving and decision-making steps, and the five themes of geography once before Unit 1. A back-matter Reference Guide (R2-R28: Atlas, Geography Terms, Picture Glossary, Index) runs as a whole-year reference. No week-by-week or day-by-day calendar is given anywhere; pacing is left to the teacher or parent, the same as the sibling Harcourt Science volume.

layer3_structure.cadence: Not stated as a weekly calendar anywhere in the sampled pages. Organized as 6 units of 4-6 lessons each (28 lessons total), each lesson 1-2 pages. No day-by-day or week-by-week schedule is printed anywhere, unlike Homa's own weekly-template curricula; a single-lesson-per-sitting cadence is implied by the format but never stated as a number of minutes or a day of the week, so recording an invented cadence here would not be honest, the same treatment the sibling Harcourt Science volume gave its own untimed lesson format

sessionLengthMinutes.note: Not stated anywhere in the sampled pages. No time language (minutes, 'short lesson', daily/weekly) was found for any lesson, unit, or feature box. Leaving this unknown rather than guessing

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: No week-by-week template exists in the source. Every lesson instead follows the same fixed shape regardless of unit: 1-2 pages of plain declarative text with 1-2 bolded vocabulary words, closing with a 'What Did You Learn?' box (2 recall questions plus 1 open reading-skill question). Each unit opens with a Begin-with-a-Song page, a Vocabulary Preview scene, and a worked example of that unit's named 'Reading Social Studies' target skill, and closes with an End-with-a-Poem/Song/Folktale page, a Unit Review, and a Discovery Channel School tie-in page. Recurring feature boxes (Citizen Heroes, Meet-the-Person biographies, Then and Now, Map and Globe Skills, Chart and Graph Skills, Here and There, DK inserts) appear roughly once or twice per lesson, each doing one distinct job rather than blending into the main lesson text
layer3_structure.progressionModel: unit-parallel rather than a single spiraling thread: the 6 units move through mostly independent social studies strands (self and school, community, work and economics, earth and resources, national civics and history, world comparison) with light internal buildup inside each unit (for example Unit 2 moves from 'what is a neighborhood' to 'kinds of communities' to 'community customs' to 'laws and leaders' to 'where my community fits in the world') but does not spiral concepts back across units the way a Charlotte Mason or classical program does; reads as a single-pass survey across six broad social studies strands for the grade, the same shape the sibling Harcourt Science volume takes across its own three science branches
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Every lesson closes with its own 'What Did You Learn?' comprehension check (2 recall questions plus 1 open reading-skill question). Each of the 6 units additionally closes with a Unit Review. No tests, quizzes, or scores were observed in any sampled page. The Social Studies Handbook and the Reference Guide (Atlas, Geography Terms, Picture Glossary, Index) function as ongoing whole-year references the child returns to, not graded checkpoints
layer3_structure.notes: Front matter includes a dedicated 'Social Studies Handbook' (pages H2-H14, its own separate page numbering before Unit 1 begins) covering citizenship vocabulary with photos (respect, caring, responsibility, fairness, honesty, courage), a 6-step problem-solving process and a 5-step decision-making process under 'Citizenship in Action,' the Five Themes of Geography illustrated with one shared example (a school building), and a Map and Globe Skills Review page (using a zoo map to practice near/far/between). This is the same front-loaded-skills-vocabulary pattern the sibling Harcourt Science volume uses for its own process-skills spread, adapted to citizenship and geography vocabulary instead of science process skills. Like the Harcourt Science and Harcourt Art Everywhere volumes in this drop wave, this is a school-classroom-market book (the front cover shows three puppet characters representing a firefighter, a chef, and another community helper; 'Citizen Heroes: Learning About Each Other' and several lesson photos show a full classroom of children); curriculum-writer should treat this the same way, a light one-adult, one-child adaptation of the comprehension-check and feature-box content rather than a literal transcription of classroom group routines.

activityTypes.description: The 2-page 'Vocabulary Preview' that opens every unit (6 across the book): one large illustrated scene (a city street, a farm, a country landscape) with the unit's key vocabulary terms labeled on circular callouts pointing to relevant parts of the scene (for example 'neighborhood,' 'community,' 'law,' 'leader,' 'state,' 'continent,' 'ocean').
activityTypes.notes: labeled-anatomy-diagram's own 'Great for' line already names 'geography (map labeling)' alongside body systems and plant parts, and its leader-line-plus-word-bank shape (or the fully-labeled reference variant, since this feature has no blank/testing version in the source) is a strong fit for a big labeled vocabulary scene.

activityTypes.description: The fixed 'What Did You Learn?' box closing every lesson (28 across the book): 2 literal recall questions plus a 3rd open 'Think and Share' or 'Write and Share' question practicing that unit's named reading-comprehension skill.
activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-21: this recurring closer box turned out to be a genuine, repeatable format shared across published elementary textbooks generally (28 occurrences in this book alone), not a one-off. New recipe file at apps/web/agent/skills/materials-studio/references/recipes/lesson-comprehension-check.md, plus a Format library row in materials-studio SKILL.md and an activity-formats.md entry, checked first against checklist-assessment, guided-notes, and structured-outline, none of which cover a fixed recall-plus-open-question lesson closer.

activityTypes.description: The recurring 'Citizen Heroes' and 'Meet [Person]' Read-Together Biography spreads (roughly 16 across the book): a short real person's story (photo, a US-location map, 2-3 paragraphs) paired with one named citizenship trait (caring, respect, responsibility, fairness, honesty, courage) and a closing reflection question ('Courage in Action,' 'Honesty in Action,' or 'Think and Share').
activityTypes.notes: Same treatment the Harcourt Science ingest recorded for its own scientist/engineer biography Links: usable but not a precise fit. artist-composer-study-card's frame-plus-bio-plus-reflection shape reuses cleanly for a citizen-hero bio, but its reflection stem and 'Where they were from' circle are written for CM-style artist study, not a citizenship-trait biography. curriculum-writer.md's new methodology section says to adapt the labels rather than use it unedited; no recipe file edit made this session for this pattern, consistent with the Harcourt Science precedent of not editing a recipe for a lower-priority reuse.

activityTypes.description: The recurring 'Then and Now' feature (4 across the book: 'How a Community Changed,' 'Changing Toys,' 'Our Country's Flag,' plus the Unit 6 grandparent-interview lesson 'How Things Have Changed'): two small panels, one showing something from the past and one showing the same thing today, each with a short caption, plus a comparison question.
activityTypes.notes: Genuine gap, built this session: no existing recipe covers a two-panel before/after time comparison (classification-sorting-mat is a category sort, not a time comparison; guided-notes is a notes layout, not an image comparison). Recurs 4 times in this book alone and is a common pattern across elementary social studies and science curricula generally (community change, invention history, life-cycle before/after), so building the recipe now rather than deferring it. New recipe file at apps/web/agent/skills/materials-studio/references/recipes/then-and-now-comparison.md, plus a Format library row in materials-studio SKILL.md and an activity-formats.md entry.

activityTypes.description: The recurring 'Map and Globe Skills' callout (6 across the book: Use a Map Key, Use Four Directions, Follow a Route, Locate Land and Water, Use a History Map, plus the front-matter Map and Globe Skills Review): a small map or globe illustration with a map key or compass rose, and 1-2 practice questions.
activityTypes.notes: Same recipe as the vocabulary-preview scene above (its 'Great for' line explicitly covers map labeling); the leader-line-plus-word-bank shape works for labeling map-key symbols or compass directions, and the three built-in scaffolding levels (fully labeled, numbered with word bank, blank for testing) map cleanly onto reference vs. practice vs. assessment versions of a map skill page.

activityTypes.description: The recurring 'Chart and Graph Skills' callout (5 across the book: Read a Calendar, Read a Time Line, Read a Diagram, Read a Bar Graph): a small chart, timeline, diagram, or bar graph with 1-2 practice questions, separate from the lesson's own comprehension check.
activityTypes.notes: RESOLVED 2026-07-21: on reflection this is a genuinely cross-subject, evergreen data-literacy skill (math, science, and social studies all use it), not a one-book callout, so it earned its own recipe rather than staying deferred. New recipe file at apps/web/agent/skills/materials-studio/references/recipes/chart-and-graph-skill-practice.md, plus a Format library row in materials-studio SKILL.md and an activity-formats.md entry, checked first against singapore-workbook-page and guided-notes, neither of which teaches a chart/graph/calendar/diagram reading skill with a worked example and practice questions.

activityTypes.description: The recurring 'Here and There' feature (3 across the book: Money Around the World, Endangered Animals, It Is Time to Leave) making one specific comparison between the child's own world and another place, with a short caption and photo.
activityTypes.notes: A loose fit reused with a caveat: nature-identification-poster's labeled-grid-of-images shape works for a simple side-by-side world comparison (for example different countries' coins, or animals from different places), though the recipe's own framing is nature-study-specific. Low volume (3 instances) and low urgency; no recipe file edit made this session.

activityTypes.description: The DK (Dorling Kindersley) inserts (3 across the book: Chinese New Year, Telephones, Big Wheels): a full-color real-world photo essay on one topic with short captions per photo, distinct from the book's own illustrated lesson style.
activityTypes.notes: A real-photograph-plus-caption grid is the closest fit; nomenclature-cards' 'realistic imagery preferred over cartoon' design pattern and image-plus-label shape reuse reasonably, though this book's own DK pages read more like a magazine layout than a card set. Low volume (3 instances); no recipe file edit made this session.

activityTypes.description: The 'Symbols in Our Country' lesson's photo-plus-caption arrangement (Washington Monument, Statue of Liberty, Liberty Bell, Bald Eagle, Gateway Arch, Alamo, and the country's motto on a coin), each symbol with a one-sentence explanation of what it stands for.
activityTypes.notes: nomenclature-cards' labeled-image-card-grid shape is a strong fit for a set of national-symbol reference cards (image, name, and what it stands for), the same way the Harcourt Science ingest reused this recipe for its glossary. No recipe file edit needed.

activityTypes.description: The back-matter Picture Glossary: roughly 90 terms A-Z, each paired with one clean real-world photo example and a page cross-reference back into the lesson content (for example 'flag: A symbol that stands for a country. The American flag is a symbol of our country. (page 16)').
activityTypes.notes: Same reasoning as the Harcourt Science ingest's glossary mapping and this book's own national-symbols mapping above: the control-card grid (image plus label) most faithfully reproduces this book's own term-plus-photo reference-card style.

activityTypes.description: The back-matter Atlas: a labeled world map (7 continents, oceans), a United States map, and an all-50-states map, each with region names as leader-line labels.
activityTypes.notes: Folded into the same map-labeling use of labeled-anatomy-diagram as the vocabulary-preview scene and Map and Globe Skills callouts above; not counted as a fourth separate mapping.

activityTypes.description: The low-volume 'Interview with a Farmer' lesson: a Q-and-A dialogue between two named speakers (a child and an adult) with photos, distinct from the book's own third-person lesson-text style.
activityTypes.notes: A single instance in this book (the grandparent conversation in 'How Things Have Changed' is similar but reads as free-flowing narration, not a labeled Q-and-A). Too low-volume to justify a dedicated recipe on its own, the same treatment the Harcourt Science ingest gave its own low-volume career-biography Links pattern; social-narrative's first-person format is the closest existing recipe if a family specifically requests this shape, though it is not a precise fit.

decisionsNeeded.item: Added 3 new social_studies topics this session, all append-only under existing MARBLE_DOMAIN_MAP pairs (History > Geography, History > Cultural Studies), no mapping.ts edit needed: mt_NlyT4Xzzr2 'Reading a Map: Map Key and Four Directions' (Geography, age 5-7), mt_Dan03VC4Li 'Kinds of Communities: City, Town, and Farm' (Geography, age 5-7), mt_OWl0pyMgMJ 'Celebrations and Traditions Around the World' (Cultural Studies, age 5-7). topics.json grew from 1640 to 1643 topics (insertions only, verified by diff); packages/taxonomy/data/manifest.json counts and topics.json bytes/sha256 updated to match; pnpm taxonomy:slugs, pnpm taxonomy:progress, and pnpm check:taxonomy all re-run and green.
decisionsNeeded.impact: History (social_studies) had zero coverage below age 9 for basic map skills, community types, or world traditions before this session; these three additions give Homa a foothold for exactly the content this Grade 1 curriculum, and likely most Grade K-2 social studies curricula, actually teaches.

decisionsNeeded.item: RESOLVED 2026-07-21 (before merge): the architecture finding below was surfaced but not acted on when this curriculum was first ingested. packages/taxonomy/src/domains.ts reserves 4 AUTHORED_DOMAINS for social_studies (family-community, geography-maps, civics-government, economics-money), already populated by a separate hand-authored milestone bank (packages/core/src/map/content.ts / item-domains.ts), not by the Marble-imported topics.json this skill edits. The fix: added two NEW content-kind MARBLE_DOMAIN_MAP entries with deliberately non-colliding ids, following the exact pattern already used for Geography and Cultural Studies earlier in this same ingest and for Art/Music in a sibling curriculum this session: 'History > Civic Life' -> domainId civic-life, and 'History > Colonial & Revolutionary America' -> domainId colonial-revolutionary-america (packages/taxonomy/src/mapping.ts). Neither collides with the reserved assessment-kind ids; check:taxonomy's 'domain ids are unique' check confirms 110 domains, 0 duplicates. This did not require resolving the deeper dual-pipeline question (whether the Marble and hand-authored bank systems should ever converge); it sidesteps the collision the same safe way the original session did for the 3 topics that already shipped.
decisionsNeeded.impact: Unblocks all 7 real per-lesson gaps that were previously left no_subject (see the next entry below, also resolved). Establishes civic-life and colonial-revolutionary-america as the durable home for this kind of Grade K-2 civics/early-American-history content in future curriculum ingests, so the next social-studies-flavored drop does not have to re-derive this.

This lets curriculum-writer apply the method's distinctive rules (name the unit's reading skill, keep the three-part What-Did-You-Learn box intact, keep each recurring feature box's own job separate rather than merging them) whenever a family uses a published reading-skill-integrated social studies textbook.

notes: Real page counts, verified directly with pypdf and PyMuPDF rather than assumed from filenames: social-studies-all-together-pt1.pdf is 120 PDF pages, social-studies-all-together-pt2.pdf is 43 PDF pages (163 PDF pages total), both CamScanner-style phone scans of the physical hardcover book with no embedded text layer at all (pypdf's extract_text returned zero characters of real content on every one of the 163 pages, confirming this is a pure image scan; all reading in this analysis was done visually from PyMuPDF-rendered page images, not from extracted text). pt1/pt2 relationship confirmed as a genuine, gapless continuation of the same physical book, not a duplicate or a distinct volume: pt1's final rendered spread (PDF page 120) shows printed pages 214-215 (the end of Unit 5 Lesson 5, 'We Celebrate Holidays,' Martin Luther King Jr. Day and Presidents' Day content), and pt2's first rendered spread (PDF page 1) shows printed page 216 ('Meet Abraham Lincoln,' the very next content), with no missing or repeated printed page numbers at the seam. Front cover (pt1 page 1) reads 'SOCIAL STUDIES, Scott Foresman, All Together' with three puppet characters (a firefighter, a chef, and a third community-helper figure); the title page (pt1 page 2) confirms 'All Together' as this specific volume's own title within the Scott Foresman Social Studies series (program authors including Dr. Candy Dawson Boyd and Dr. Geneva Gay), not a Harcourt-branded book despite two sibling Grade 1 Harcourt volumes (Harcourt Art Everywhere, Harcourt Science) arriving in the same drop wave; the copyright page (pt1 page 3) confirms 'Copyright (c) 2003 by Pearson Education, Inc.,' ISBN 0-328-01759-0. Full table of contents sampled directly (pt1 pages 3-6): 6 units (Unit 1 Time for School; Unit 2 In My Community; Unit 3 Work! Work! Work!; Unit 4 Our Earth, Our Resources; Unit 5 This Is Our Country; Unit 6 Our Country, Our World), Reference Guide (Atlas R2, Geography Terms R10, Picture Glossary R12, Index R24). Grade level is Grade 1, determined from internal content evidence as instructed, not assumed from the drain order or the two sibling Harcourt Grade 1 volumes' own findings: (1) the 'Citizen Heroes: Ruby Bridges Hall' biography states directly 'Ruby was six years old when she began first grade,' presented as a same-age peer figure for the reader; (2) every lesson's reading passage uses very short, simple declarative sentences ('My neighborhood is part of a community. A community is a group of people and the place where they live.'; 'I have jobs at school. My big job is to learn.'), consistent with an early-elementary supported reader, the same reading level the sibling Harcourt Science and Harcourt Art Everywhere Grade 1 volumes show; (3) every lesson's 'What Did You Learn?' box requires full sentence-level comprehension responses (recall questions plus an open Think-and-Share or Write-and-Share question), a demand level well beyond a Kindergarten book; (4) cross-referencing this curriculum's own content against Homa's taxonomy, the closest-matching existing Homa topics cluster tightly at ages 5-7 across every unit (Rules and agreements exist 5-7, Needs & Wants 5-7, Goods & Services 5-7, Buyers & Sellers 5-7, Local weather patterns 5-6), consistent with a 6-7-year-old reader, the same age cluster the sibling volumes' own Grade 1 findings showed. Unlike the Harcourt Art series (where 'Art Everywhere' vs other subtitles distinguishes grade level directly in the cover title), this book's cover reads only 'Social Studies, All Together' with no explicit numeral, so grade level rests entirely on the internal content evidence above, the same situation the sibling Harcourt Science volume was in. Sampling covered the front cover, title page, copyright page, full table of contents, and front-matter Social Studies Handbook (pt1 PDF pages 1-16); Unit 1's full lesson set and Citizen Heroes: Ruby Bridges Hall (pt1 pages 17-40); Unit 2's Vocabulary Preview, Different Kinds of Communities, Chinese New Year DK insert, and End with a Poem (pt1 pages 46-53, 66, 74, 80-81); Unit 3's Welcome to Job Day, Interview with a Farmer, and From Place to Place (pt1 pages 108-109, 116-117, 124-125); Unit 4's Begin with a Song and Our Earth's Resources (pt1 pages 90, 144-145, 156-157); Unit 5's Meet Benjamin Franklin, We Celebrate Holidays, Symbols in Our Country, and Choosing Our Country's Leaders (pt1 pages 110, 115-119); the Unit 5/pt2 seam and Meet Abraham Lincoln (pt2 pages 0-1); Choosing Our Country's Leaders continuation (pt2 page 1); Unit 6's Begin with a Song, Eleanor Roosevelt, How Things Have Changed, and Telephones DK insert (pt2 pages 3-4, 8, 13, 17); Kay's Grandparents Reading Social Studies feature and Meet Mae Jemison (pt2 pages 20, 22); and the back-matter Atlas, Picture Glossary, Index, and Credits (pt2 pages 30, 35, 40, 42). This is representative sampling across the full breadth of both files as instructed, not a page-by-page read of all 163 PDF pages. Copyrighted page images and the publisher's specific passage wording were used only for this session's own analysis and are described here in Homa's own words, never reproduced verbatim into any product file; the new taxonomy topics, the then-and-now-comparison recipe, and the curriculum-writer methodology section describe generic elementary-social-studies concepts and page-layout patterns in Homa's own voice, not a copy of this publisher's specific text, photos, or layout.
